Przykładowo ceny części serwerów Dedibox wzrosły o około 12 do 17%. Dedibox Core 10 M podrożał z 299,99 do 349,99 euro miesięcznie, natomiast Core 10 S z 199,99 do 229,99 euro. Scaleway podniósł również ceny magazynowania danych i równoważenia obciążenia.

results.title: EU Sovereign Cloud Providers Pay Spot Prices on Chips
results.author: Andrei Nutas
highlights:
On 10 August 2026, Octave Klaba, the founder and chairman of OVHcloud, one of Europe’s largest independent cloud providers, posted the company’s new prices in a thread on X. Almost everything is going up. The steepest increases fall on the newest dedicated servers, which will cost as much as 87 percent more, and the rises run down the whole catalogue from there, through older machines and into public cloud instances. New orders reprice on 1 September. Renewals follow a month later.

Behind the increases is the cost of memory. Since 1 July, adding RAM to a new OVHcloud order costs 127 percent more, and adding storage 89 percent more. By Klaba’s account, DRAM and NAND prices have risen roughly sixfold year on year through June, he projects ninefold by September and twelvefold by 2027, and the reason is that the manufacture of GPUs and high-bandwidth memory for AI has pulled fabrication capacity away from the ordinary components every server is built around.

...

For comparison, Amazon buys DRAM and NAND in the same overheated market. Yet so far its prices have barely moved. It has raised EC2 Capacity Blocks for ML, one reserved GPU product, by about 20 percent from July on top of roughly 15 percent in January, and left everything else untouched, including instances running Trainium, the accelerator it designs itself. This was also done without an announcement. The new numbers appeared on the pricing page, and after Business Insider reported them AWS said only that Capacity Blocks prices “are updated periodically based on supply and demand.”

Amazon can hold its prices because it designs its own accelerators and because it buys memory years in advance, in volumes big enough that suppliers serve it first. None of the European providers has those options. Klaba described OVHcloud’s own position in the same thread, placing orders “month by month, over 12 months, with no guarantee of the purchase price and without knowing what will be the real demand from our customers.” There is no reason to think StackIT, IONOS, Scaleway or Hetzner, the other European Cloud providers, buy on better terms.

results.title: Fireworks is raising on-demand GPU prices up to 30% on September 1 | Beyond the News
highlights:
# Fireworks is raising on-demand GPU prices up to 30% on September 1

Fireworks' current pricing table shows September 1 increases across H100, H200, B200, B300 and GB300 on-demand deployments, with B200 rising from $10 to $13 per GPU-hour. Dedicated training jobs that use the same GPU-hour rates inherit the new economics.

Reviewed and published by Lars Jansen Updated 28 Aug 2026, 10:59 pm NZST 4 min read Copy link

 First published 28 Aug 2026, 10:59 pm NZST 

## Key details

1. The new Fireworks on-demand GPU rates begin September 1, 2026.
2. H100 80GB: $7 → $8 per GPU-hour.
3. H200 141GB: $7 → $8 per GPU-hour.
4. B200 180GB: $10 → $13 per GPU-hour.
5. B300 288GB: $12 → $15 per GPU-hour.
6. GB300 288GB: $18 → $20 per GPU-hour.
7. On-demand deployments are billed per GPU second with no extra startup charges.
8. Region-restricted deployments are priced at a 1.5× premium.
9. Dedicated Training API jobs use the same on-demand GPU-hour pricing.

...

## What changed

Fireworks' current pricing page publishes a two-column transition for its on-demand GPU deployments: prices through August 31 and new rates from September 1, 2026. H100 80GB and H200 141GB increase from $7 to $8 per GPU-hour; B200 180GB rises from $10 to $13; B300 288GB from $12 to $15; and GB300 288GB from $18 to $20. Fireworks bills on-demand deployments per GPU second with no startup charge, and its Dedicated Training API uses the same GPU-hour pricing, so the change affects both dedicated serving and GPU-hour training jobs. Region-restricted deployments continue to carry a 1.5× premium.

...

Dedicated GPU economics can dominate the unit cost of high-volume inference, fine-tuning and reinforcement-learning workloads. These increases range from roughly 11% to 30%, large enough to change break-even points between accelerator generations, serverless APIs and competing GPU clouds. The biggest increase is on B200, where a workload consuming 1,000 GPU-hours per month moves from $10,000 to $13,000 before regional premiums or other services. Teams should therefore benchmark completed-task throughput rather than choosing hardware on hourly price or peak specifications alone.

## The September increase varies materially by accelerator

H100 and H200 move from $7 to $8 per hour, about a 14.3% increase. B200 rises 30% from $10 to $13, B300 rises 25% from $12 to $15 and GB300 rises about 11.1% from $18 to $20. The uneven changes can alter the relative cost ranking of GPUs even when performance remains unchanged.

...

On-demand deployments are billed by the second and do not charge extra startup time, which remains useful for bursty workloads. But sustained fleets still absorb the full hourly increase, and a region-restricted deployment costs 1.5 times the listed rate.

results.title: Cheapest H100 and B200 Cloud: CoreWeave vs Nebius vs Lambda vs Crusoe · Aliteq
results.author: Aliteq Team
highlights:
On each provider's own pricing page on Nov 3, 2026, Crusoe had the cheapest on-demand H100 ($3.90 a GPU-hour, rising to $4.50 on Dec 1) and Lambda the cheapest B200 ($6.69). CoreWeave was the most expensive on demand, but its fixed spot prices undercut everyone's on-demand rate. The full table, the catches, and where the marketplace tier sits.

...

Which big GPU cloud is cheapest for H100 and B200? On each provider's own pricing page on November 3, 2026: for the H100, Crusoe at $3.90 per GPU-hour on demand, with Lambda a cent behind at $3.99 on an 8-GPU instance. For the B200, Lambda at $6.69 per GPU-hour (8x), well under Nebius ($8.50) and CoreWeave ($8.60). CoreWeave is the most expensive on demand, but if your job can be interrupted its published spot prices ($2.46 an H100, $4.26 a B200, per GPU) undercut everyone's on-demand rate. Two dates to know: Crusoe's own page says its H100 goes to $4.50 on December 1, 2026, which hands the cheapest on-demand H100 to Lambda.

## The short answer (read Nov 3, 2026)

Among CoreWeave, Nebius, Lambda and Crusoe, the cheapest on-demand H100 on November 3, 2026 was Crusoe at $3.90 per GPU-hour, then Lambda at $3.99 (8x instance), Nebius at $4.50 and CoreWeave at $6.16 (an 8-GPU node at $49.24 an hour). Crusoe's page says its H100 rises to $4.50 on December 1, 2026. The cheapest on-demand B200 was Lambda at $6.69 per GPU-hour (8x; $6.99 on one GPU), then Nebius at $8.50 and CoreWeave at $8.60; Crusoe's B200 is contact-sales. For interruptible work, CoreWeave's spot nodes work out to $2.46 per H100 and $4.26 per B200, and Nebius preemptible starts from $0.79 (H100) and $0.99 (B200) at a dynamic rate. Smaller clouds go lower still: Hyperstack listed a B200 at $6.00 and an H100 at $2.50.

...

- H100 on demand, per GPU-hour, Nov 3, 2026: Crusoe $3.90, Lambda $3.99 (8x) to $4.29 (1x SXM), Nebius $4.50, CoreWeave $6.16.

results.title: The Cloud GPU Price War 2026: Neoclouds vs Hyperscalers
highlights:
- Neoclouds list an on-demand H100 from ~$2.89/hr (RunPod) to ~$3.99/hr (Together AI); Nebius lists $3.85/GPU-hr

- One Aug 2026 report puts neocloud rentals up to 66% below the large incumbent clouds
- But contract prices rose: SemiAnalysis' H100 1-year index climbed from ~$1.70 (Oct 2025) toward ~$2.35/GPU-hr (Mar 2026)
- CoreWeave raised list prices ~25% across SKUs in July 2026 and called capacity “effectively sold out”
- AWS quietly raised H200 Capacity Block prices ~15% on Jan 4, 2026 — reportedly its first EC2 GPU price increase in ~two decades
- Nebius disclosed a capacity auction clearing 15% above its highest-ever Blackwell price
- Net: spot/older-Hopper pricing softened; premium, reserved, and Blackwell pricing firmed or rose

...

AWS — ~15% H200 Capacity Block increase (Jan 4, 2026)

AWS raised prices on its H200 EC2 Capacity Blocks by roughly 15% effective January 4, 2026 — p5e.48xlarge reportedly moved from $34.61 to $39.80/hr — without a formal customer announcement, in what multiple outlets described as its first EC2 GPU price increase in roughly two decades of EC2 pricing (GIGAZINE, Jan 7, 2026). Treat the exact figures as multiply-reported rather than primary-confirmed.

results.title: temperature2 ships /gpu/: what compute actually costs
results.author: The Hardware Desk
highlights:
temperature2's /gpu/ section charts daily GPU rental prices in US dollars per GPU-hour for the H100 SXM, H200, B200, A100 SXM4 and RTX 5090, alongside blended token prices in dollars per million tokens for Anthropic, OpenAI, Google and DeepSeek, both from the Ornn Data public index, plus depreciation, volatility, generational premium and breakeven figures computed from those series.

 TL;DR 

- ▸ An H100 SXM hour settled at $2.68 on 26 August 2026, a B200 hour at $6.22 and an RTX 5090 hour at $0.54 — 92 days of daily settlements, all charted.
- ▸ Token prices fell far harder than rent this month: OpenAI's blended price is down 68.0% over 31 days while H100 rent moved -1.5%.
- ▸ The board carries volatility, rebased depreciation curves, generational ratios and $/PFLOP-hour, all computed here from the published series with the method written next to each number.
- ▸ One GPU-hour has to produce 1.83M tokens to cover its own rent at Anthropic's blended price and 26.15M at DeepSeek's — a 14.28x spread in what a token is worth.
- ▸ Prices are from the Ornn Data public index; the public window is rolling, so the site keeps its own archive and never rewrites a recorded day.

...

## The board

Five GPUs, one row each, 92 days of daily settlements from 27 May to 26 August 2026.

| GPU | USD/hour | 92d | Volatility | Range | $/PFLOP-hr |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| B200 | $6.22 | +17.1% | 60% | $4.22 – $7.28 | $2.76 |
| H200 | $4.24 | +8.7% | 97% | $2.99 – $5.62 | $4.29 |
| H100 SXM | $2.68 | -2.9% | 63% | $2.29 – $3.17 | $2.71 |
| A100 SXM4 | $1.06 | -14.5% | 39% | $0.99 – $1.31 | $3.40 |
| RTX 5090 | $0.54 | -37.2% | 74% | $0.48 – $1.33 | $2.58 |

Prices settled 26 August 2026, Ornn Data Compute Price Index. Volatility is the annualized standard deviation of daily log returns scaled by the square root of 365 — calendar days rather than trading days, because compute rents on weekends and a 252-day scaling would understate it by about 17%. That measure, the changes, the ranges and the per-unit columns are all computed on this site from the published daily series, not read from a paid analytics endpoint, which is why the method can be stated instead of cited.

...

Absolute dollars hide the slope, and the slope is the story.

results.title: Financing the AI Boom 3 - by Marc Rubinstein - Net Interest
results.author: Marc Rubinstein
highlights: Yet they are. According to Silicon Data, the price to rent a Nvidia Hopper H100 chip for an hour has risen to $2.71, up from $1.96 at the end of November. And there’s no sign of a slowdown. Forward rates compiled by Silicon Data (more on them later) curve upwards into 2027 and 2028. One rental customer, Baseten, a provider of software and computing capacity to companies tapping into lower-cost AI models, revealed recently that its cloud service provider will push up the rental price on its Nvidia Blackwell B200 GPUs from $2.63 per hour to $5.10 when its contract renews in October.
